title: Ethiopian Chechebsa Street Version
community: Addis Ababa street food — the breakfast scramble sold at stalls
author: Chef Haile
desc: Addis Ababa Street Chechebsa — kita bread torn and tossed in a street stall's large flat pan with kibbeh and berbere, plated with a fried egg on top. The street breakfast version of the home dish — faster, more dramatic, eaten standing at the stall.
longDesc: Street Chechebsa is what Addis Ababa morning food culture produces — the home dish of torn kita in kibbeh taken to street scale, the large flat pan (mitad) cooking enormous quantities, a fried egg always placed on top, eaten standing at the stall before work.
steps: Heat kibbeh in a large flat pan until hot.
Add berbere. Stir 30 seconds in the hot kibbeh.
Add torn kita pieces. Toss vigorously to coat every piece.
Cook 3—4 minutes, tossing, until every piece is spiced and slightly crisped.
In a separate pan, fry eggs sunny-side up.
Plate chechebsa. Top with fried egg. Sprinkle mitmita.
chefTips: Street chechebsa is always hotter than home chechebsa — more berbere.
The fried egg is the street version addition — non-negotiable.
commonMistakes: Not enough kibbeh — the coating is the point.
cookingScience: See ETH010 for Chechebsa cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Street stall cooking on a single mitad — very energy efficient at scale.
culturalNote: Street Chechebsa is the Addis Ababa morning ritual — the breakfast stall with the mitad, the cloud of berbere-kibbeh steam rising in the morning air, the crowd of workers and students eating standing before heading to their day. It is urban Ethiopian life at its most immediate.
